_comment: Single source of truth for Arcade Battle Royale constants that were previously hand-duplicated across server/server.js, client/src/pages/Arcade/ArcadeBattleRoyale.jsx, and client/src/pages/Arcade/bot/*.js. Both the server (CommonJS require) and the client/bot bundle (Vite ESM import) load this same JSON file directly. Edit values ONLY here; do not reintroduce local copies.
_quickModeComment: Phase 8.4 alternate pacing, chosen at room creation. Same phase sequence as the standard mode, just shorter, so nothing downstream needs to know which mode a room is in beyond looking up its durations. Rooms store their choice in arcade_rooms.round_duration_mode and every timing decision reads the room's own table rather than a global constant.
_difficultyComment: Phase 8.4 task source for Rounds 1-3. 'default' keeps the three fixed built-in tasks every match has always used; easy/medium/hard instead draw from the arcade_tasks DB pool by difficulty, the same way Round 4 already does.
_autoSubmitLeadSecondsComment: How many seconds before a round's deadline the client auto-submits for a player who never pressed submit. It cannot be 0: submitMyRound() runs the player's code through Pyodide and then calls the AI code-quality judge before it POSTs, which takes several seconds, and POST /submit-round rejects anything arriving once the server has already finalized the round. Firing exactly at 0 therefore always lost the round (observed live 2026-08-17: an unsubmitted round wrote no history row and scored 0). Keep this comfortably above the judging pipeline's worst-case latency.
_autoSubmitWarnSecondsComment: Countdown value at which the player is warned that their answer is about to be auto-submitted. Must be LARGER than autoSubmitLeadSeconds — warning them at the exact moment the submission fires is not a warning. The gap is the reaction time a player gets to finish a thought and press submit themselves.
_roundHistoryComment: Phase 8.3/Step 5 retention. Round history is deliberately NO LONGER tied to arcade_rooms by a cascading foreign key: rooms are deleted the moment they empty, which meant a player lost the ability to review their own code the instant they left the match. History now outlives the room, so it needs its own bound instead — each player keeps their most recent N matches and older ones are swept.
_beginnerBudgetComment: The problem bank is drawn against the clock, not blindly. arcade_tasks.work_chars records how many characters of the finished answer a player still has to type once starter_code is on screen; drawArcadeRoundTasks() keeps only problems whose work_chars fits (roundSeconds - autoSubmitLeadSeconds) at this typing rate. 90 chars/min is a beginner writing CODE, which is far slower than prose because of symbols, indentation and editor navigation. Measured 2026-08-19: without this filter a beginner could not physically type 70% of the bank inside Quick Mode's usable seconds, so rounds were being lost to keystrokes rather than to thinking. Raising this number makes the draw more permissive, not the players faster.
_finalePoolComment: Which difficulty Round 4 - the elimination finale - is drawn from, per the room's own chosen difficulty. Round 4 used to be hardcoded to 'hard' for every room, which meant an easy room's decider was a problem nobody in it could finish, so the round scored everyone equally at zero and decided nothing. The finale is still always at least as hard as Rounds 1-3; it just climbs with the room instead of jumping straight to the top.
_exampleCasesComment: How many of a problem's test cases are shown to the player as worked input/output examples. Beginners were being asked to infer the exact shape of a return value from prose alone. Deliberately fewer than a problem has, so the examples cannot be turned into a hardcoded lookup table that passes the hidden remainder.
_botSkillComment: How strong the synthesized bot opponents are, per room difficulty. Bot scores used to come from one fixed band regardless of the room, so choosing an easy room made the problems easier but left the opposition exactly as strong - an easy room was not actually easier to survive. 'medium' reproduces that original band exactly, so any change in behaviour is attributable to the room's own setting. passMin/passSpread are the fraction of test cases a bot passes; qualityMin/qualitySpread are its code-quality score out of 100.
_botPacingComment: Bot decision pacing, in wall-clock milliseconds. These exist because bot behaviour used to be driven purely by how often botManager.update() happened to be called: buying and item-use were bare per-call probability gates, so when a render-loop bug ran the tick at ~164Hz the bots attempted thousands of purchases per shop and emptied their whole bag within milliseconds of a round starting. Fixing the loop to 1Hz silently re-balanced the entire game. Gating on elapsed time instead makes bot pacing identical no matter how often the tick runs — including when a browser throttles a backgrounded tab.
_scoreSubmissionComment: Upper bound on a round score the server will accept from a client. The server has no Python runtime, so it cannot re-run the player's code — it takes the client's word for the score, the same trust boundary the learning-system exercises use. That was fine for a solo exercise and is not fine here: an Arcade round score feeds match ranking, elimination, and the permanent arcade_player_stats record, and the previous ceiling of 999,999,999 meant a hand-edited request could win every match forever. The real maximum a round can produce is 600 (three components of 100, tripled by the equal-weight sum to 300, doubled by scoreMultiplier); 10000 leaves deliberate headroom above that. Note what this does and does not buy: it stops absurd values and keeps the stats table sane, but a determined cheater can still post 10000 and top the board. Narrowing it later is a one-value change here.
_matchTickComment: Pacing for the server-side match clock (tickArcadeMatches). The tick is the sole authority on phase/timer/score/elimination, so it must keep running - but it must also stop hammering a database that is not there. When postgres restarted underneath the server on 2026-08-18 the tick retried every 1000ms forever and logged 56,492 identical errors before the process died, which buried the one line that actually said what happened. On consecutive failures the delay now doubles from tickIntervalMs up to tickMaxBackoffMs, and resets the instant a tick succeeds. Nothing is lost by backing off: while the database is unreachable no phase can be advanced anyway, and every room's phase_deadline is a timestamp, so once it recovers the overdue rooms are all picked up on the next successful tick.
_staleParticipantSecondsComment: How long a real player can go without a heartbeat poll before the server treats them as disconnected. GET /rooms/:id is the heartbeat and normally runs every 2s, but browsers throttle timers in backgrounded tabs down to roughly one wake per minute, so a player who merely switches tabs mid-match must not look disconnected. This has to stay comfortably above that once-a-minute floor.
_coinRewardComment: Gold paid into users.virtual_currency when a match reaches RESULT, by finishing rank. This is the same wallet the lessons and the shop use — every mode pays into it and cosmetics are bought out of it. Calibrated against the learning rewards, which give 5-10 coins per exercise: winning a four-round match is worth about five exercises. Ranks past the list get coinRewardParticipation. Bots are never paid, and a player whose arcade name has no account is skipped.
